verdicts.note: Hertz rule: generic US-wide TSA 'know your rights' guide; American Samoa is never mentioned and is not a subject. Its screening facts describe the FEDERAL framework that belongs sourced in the USA parent record. Under the new rule, 'TSA operates there' is not a relevance argument.

Wrong jurisdiction: the article's subject is a Kansas statute (birth-certificate/DL invalidation, bathroom ban). ASM not mentioned. BUT it contains a federally-applicable fact worth re-sourcing at intake: 'US Supreme Court recently allowed the State Dept to stop processing passports with nonbinary or non-assignment markers' (dated 2026-03-03; points to HRW's 2025-11-10 dispatch as the proper citation).

verdicts.rewritten_summary: UH Manoa libraries research guide on Pacific gender identities (maintained; last updated 2026-07-23). Contains substantive American Samoa content: the Society of Fa'afafine in American Samoa (SOFIAS) was formed in 2010 by merging the American Samoa Island Queens Association and the American 7s Association, explicitly re-anchored to cultural pride - 'we are fa'afafine Samoa'. It defines fa'afafine as born male but embodying both male and female traits, 'a recognized and integral part of traditional Samoan culture', and frames colonial suppression followed by contemporary reclaiming of Pacific gender identities.
verdicts.note: Previous claim summary undersold this page (the ASM section is more than a name in a list). Supports the summary's fa'afafine/tradition paragraph, not legal status.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Out Traveler 'Ask the Expert' column (Ed Salvato, 2009-07-01) answering a honeymoon question about American Samoa: the two Samoan nations share the fa'amatai chiefly system; ASM's ~57,000 residents across seven islands/atolls; 'Samoan culture tends toward traditionalism, and reserved behavior by people of all orientations is expected', yet 'unlike the homophobia rampant in Fiji, homosexuality is a widely accepted part of Samoan culture', with Western gay men reportedly courted by fa'afafine transgender locals and by officially straight men; local artist Dan Taulapapa McMullin calls the Samoan islands 'the homeland of fa'afafine culture'; ASM hotels skew business-travel (Tradewinds, Pago Pago).
verdicts.note: Dated 2009 social/visitor color with the ANSWER included (previous summary omitted it - the answer is the point). Supports traditionalism + fa'afafine acceptance claims; no legal content.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: The Independent, 2015-07-10: American Samoa was the only US territory unsure whether Obergefell applied - AG Talauega Eleasalo Ale: 'We're still reviewing the decision to determine its applicability to American Samoa... I don't know. We're reviewing the law', while Puerto Rico, USVI, Guam and CNMI moved to apply it. ~50,000 residents, conservative Christian, motto 'Samoa, Muia God e Muamua'. Fa'afafine tradition noted; leading figure Princess Auvaa says many fa'afafine don't push gay marriage out of respect for culture/religion, yet would herself be first to apply for a licence. No same-sex marriage licence applications had been made; territorial-law experts (Villazor, Keitner) said recognition required voluntary adoption or litigation, warning the review had a chilling effect.
verdicts.note: Core marriage-status source, but 11 years old - it establishes the 2015 anomaly, NOT the current position. The record summary's 'long the one territory...' phrasing correctly hedges to past tense; freshness/intake must supply post-2015 status.

summary_assessment: Current ASM summary is only partly supported by these five links: 2015 marriage ambiguity + fa'afafine/traditionalism paragraphs check out (Independent, Manoa, Out Traveler), but 'decriminalised in the early 1980s', 'no local non-discrimination shield', 'local constitution defines marriage traditionally' and '2025-26 federal document friction' have NO backing in any retained source - they came from freshness research and need proper dated citations via intake; two of the five links fail the Hertz rule entirely.
